Mianserin Hydrochloride (BANM, USAN, rINNM) Hidrocloruro de mianserina; Mianseriinihydrokloridi; Mianserin Hidroklorür; Miansérine, chlorhydrate de; Mianserin-hydrochlo- rid; Mianserinhydroklorid; Mianserini hydrochloridum; Mianseri- no hidrochloridas; Mianseryny chlorowodorek; Mianszerin-hid- roklorid; Org-GB-94. 1,2,3,4,10,14b-Hexahydro-2-methyldiben- zo[c,f]pyrazino[1,2-a]azepine hydrochloride. Миансерина Гидрохлорид C18H20N2,HCl = 300.8. CAS — 24219-97-4 (mianserin); 21535-47-7 (mianserin hydrochloride). ATC — N06AX03. ATC Vet — QN06AX03. (mianserin) Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Mianserin Hydrochloride). A white or almost white crystalline powder or crystals. Sparingly soluble in water; slight- ly soluble in alcohol; soluble in dichloromethane. A 1% solution in water has a pH of 4.0 to 5.5. Protect from light. Adverse Effects Antimuscarinic and cardiac adverse effects are fewer and milder with mianserin, a tetracyclic antidepressant, than with tricyclic antidepressants but effects are otherwise broadly similar (see Amitriptyline, p.376); mianserin may be associated with a lower risk of cardiotoxicity in overdosage. The most common adverse effect associated with mianserin is drowsiness. Mianserin also causes bone-marrow depression usu- ally presenting as leucopenia, granulocytopenia, or agranulocy- tosis; aplastic anaemia has been reported. These adverse haema- tological reactions generally occur during the first few weeks of therapy and especially in the elderly. Other adverse effects reported include disturbances of liver func- tion and jaundice, breast disorders (gynaecomastia, nipple ten- derness, and non-puerperal lactation), and polyarthropathy. Effects on the blood.
